text: Writing clean code is a skill that every programmer should develop. The goal is not just to make the computer understand your code, but also to make it easy for other people—and your future self—to read. One of the most important habits is using clear naming conventions. Instead of calling a variable `x` or `data`, choose names that explain their purpose, like `userEmail` or `totalPrice`. Additionally, it is best to keep functions short and focused on a single task. This makes the code more maintainable because you can fix or update one small part without breaking the whole system. In the end, clean code saves time and reduces frustration.
